description: Put vehicle images into web pages, apps, emails and documents: create 1-50 key-free signed URLs a browser loads directly (), each with ready-to-display Markdown. In ChatGPT, use this tool to show the inline image card. In other chat hosts, get_car_image displays the picture inline. For chat use ttl_seconds 604800, max_uses 0 and renewal off unless requested. When ChatGPT shows the card, do not repeat its images or URLs. Without a card, use the returned Markdown where supported or link the same URL. Reuse unexpired URLs; never mint twice for one image. Each URL counts its vehicle image for the month at creation (1 credit on the legacy credit meter); loads within the TTL add nothing and are publicly cacheable. Each image names its vehicle like get_car_image: look each distinct vehicle up once (resolve_vehicle, search_vehicles or decode_vin, all free) and pass its id as vehicle, or send make, model and year in catalog spelling. Each takes any paint color (a preset or a hex) and the same sizing options (width, height, fit, background, framing, trim, padding, shadow); format auto makes the URL serve webp or png per viewer. For email, CMS pages or documents that outlive a TTL, set renew: true with ttl_seconds 604800: the URL keeps serving past expiry, renewing in each opened week (one more credit per week on the legacy credit meter), for up to renew_days. Pass idempotency_key when the call might be repeated: a retry with the same key and arguments replays the first result instead of billing again. Returns id, url, markdown, expires_at, max_uses, renews_until and the normalized vehicle for each image. Prefer this over get_car_image for HTML, Markdown files, documents, emails and websites. State expiry briefly.

idempotency_key.description: Makes a retry safe. The same key with the same arguments within 24 hours replays the first result (idempotent_replayed: true) instead of minting and billing again; the same key with different arguments is refused; a retry that overtakes a call still running is told to wait. Pass one whenever the call might be repeated, e.g. one per listing or batch.

images.description: One to fifty image requests. Each URL counts its vehicle image (vehicle, color, angle) for the month when created; the same image again this month adds nothing.

aspect_ratio.description: A preset for the box: 1:1, 4:3, 3:2 or 16:9, at the resolution you name or the largest the image allows; natural = the car's own trimmed shape. With width or height it completes the other; both together win. Never with size.

background.description: Solid background: a hex color such as "#f4f4f4" or a CSS color name such as "white" or "whitesmoke". Omit for transparent (jpg is white).

color.description: Paint color: one of the presets (white, black, gray, silver, blue, red, green, brown, beige, tan, orange, yellow, gold, burgundy, purple), a CSS color name such as navy (grey is the gray preset) or a hex like #1a2b3c. Responses echo any paint but a preset as #rrggbb.

fit.description: With width and height: contain (default) keeps the whole car and pads the rest; cover fills the box and crops; inside may return a smaller image.

format.description: png keeps the transparent background (default); webp is smallest; jpg is flattened onto white; auto lets each viewer's Accept header choose webp or png, negotiated on every load of a signed URL. An inline image (get_car_image) is delivered as png for auto.

framing.description: Composition preset, instead of trim/padding (never with them): consistent (default) keeps one apparent scale across the vehicle's views, for galleries and spinners; tight = trim with no margin, the car fills the box; balanced = trim with a 6% margin, for catalog grids and listings.

height.description: Explicit height in px (a size above the stored image's own is clamped, see width).

make.description: Manufacturer, e.g. "Porsche", "BMW", "Toyota". Case and punctuation do not matter. Prefer vehicle; omit when it is given.

model.description: Model as the catalog spells it, e.g. "911", "M3", "mx-5". Look it up (resolve_vehicle, search_vehicles) rather than typing it from memory: prefer vehicle. Conservative typos and reviewed vehicle-db aliases are accepted; BMW petrol badges preserve explicit bodies (430-gran-coupe). Matches must exist for the requested make/year; ambiguous matches remain 404s. Omit when vehicle is given.

padding.description: Margin around the image, percent of its longer side (0-50): around the car with trim, around the stored frame without it.

resolution.description: A preset for the longer side of the box: small=640, medium=1280, hd=1920, 2k=2560 px, delivered up to the stored image's own size. width or height win. Never with size.

shadow.description: Add a soft ground shadow under the car, drawn from its cut-out (semi-transparent, or grey on a background). Same image, nothing extra.

size.description: Square size preset: thumb=256, small=512, medium=768, large=1024 px. Omit for the stored image's full size.

trim.description: Crop to the car's own bounds before sizing, so it fills the box instead of floating in the frame.

vehicle.description: Stable vehicle id such as veh_395yw8tn73ff8, as resolve_vehicle (params.vehicle_id), search_vehicles and decode_vin return it. The preferred way to name a vehicle: it cannot be misspelled. It names the make, model and year, so omit those when it is given.

view.description: Camera angle, in yaw order around the car: front (0°), front-3-4 (35°, the classic hero angle, nose left), side (profile, nose left), rear-3-4 (145°, nose left), rear (180°), rear-3-4-right (215°, nose right), side-right (profile, nose right), front-3-4-right (325°, the hero angle mirrored, nose right), then top (straight down from above, nose up: a bird's-eye plan view).

width.description: Explicit width in px; overrides size. With height too, the output is exactly width x height. Delivered up to the stored image's own size, 1024 px square for older renders, up to 2560 px for new ones: a larger size is clamped, a box shrinking whole and keeping its shape (1920 x 1080 of a 1024 px image is delivered as 1024 x 576).

year.description: Model year, e.g. 2024. The catalog covers 1990 through next year. Omit when vehicle is given.

max_uses.description: Maximum redemptions per URL, 0 to 1000; 0 (default) means unlimited until expiry.

renew.description: Auto-renew past the TTL: the first load in each further window of ttl_seconds renews the URL, until renew_days (no extra count on a plan; one more credit per window on the legacy credit meter, so pair with ttl_seconds 604800). Use for email, CMS pages and documents that outlive a TTL. Requires max_uses 0.

renew_days.description: How long a renewable URL keeps renewing, 1 to 365 days from creation (default 365). Only with renew: true.

ttl_seconds.description: How long the URLs stay valid, 60 to 604800 seconds (7 days). Default 3600.
